content:
amy: Heads-up  linkcheck started failing after migration for headings with HTML entities and soft-hyphens. Old deep-links to #api-rate-limits are 404.

ben: I can repro. Docusaurus slugifier treats `—` and literal em-dash differently. Also saw soft-hyphen U+00AD embedded in some vendor files.

rafa: Quick patch idea: run unicode NFC normalization + strip soft-hyphens before slugify. I'll sketch a small plugin and tests. PR 4977.

lee: For safety, add a `--emit-redirects` mode that scans git history and outputs a redirects snippet for common legacy slugs.

docbot: linkcheck: docs/api/rate-limits.md 6 broken fragments (branch/4977). Report: https://ci.redwood-inference.local/links/4977

amy: Plan: rafa implements plugin + flag, lee adds collector script `tools/collect_slugs.py --emit`, then we enable on staging, run full linkcheck, and decide redirects.

ben: FYI also test on macOS vs Linux; mac filesystems normalize differently and can hide NFC/NFD problems.

rafa: Added tests for entities, soft-hyphen, and emoji. Perf hit is tiny (~8ms/page). Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4977 (WIP).

lee: After staging pass, we'll flip flag in prod during a maintenance window and post a changelog note. Support will watch for anchor 404s for 72h.

amy: Thanks all. If redirects count < 50 we'll emit them; otherwise we'll prioritize updating legacy files.
